decision: Require multiple individually-qualified contention runs to demonstrate bounded cross-run p95 drift before using lock/commit timings as performance evidence.
problem: A single spawned process-boundary campaign can pass absolute lock-wait and durable-commit ceilings because of favorable scheduler, filesystem, cache, or fsync conditions. Using one run to set or justify tighter budgets risks overfitting to noise.

correctness.preferred: Cross-run stability evaluation over the same enqueue, claim, and journal p95 metrics that already gate one campaign.
correctness.reason: It preserves the current correctness invariants while distinguishing repeatable performance from one lucky execution.

robustness_security.preferred: Fail closed unless every run is individually contention-ready and uses identical budgets.
robustness_security.reason: Mixing failed runs or different budget policies can manufacture an apparently stable aggregate and obscure degraded durability behavior.

latency_resources_regression.preferred: Offline comparison of existing summaries with a minimum of three sequential campaigns.
latency_resources_regression.reason: It adds no production, Qubes, or network overhead and avoids parallel self-contention that would contaminate the measurement we are trying to qualify.

alternatives_rejected: Treat one contention campaign as sufficient: lowest runtime cost but vulnerable to scheduler/fsync noise and false confidence.
Run repeated campaigns in parallel: faster wall-clock but creates artificial host contention and corrupts the latency comparison.

Move immediately to a database or lock daemon: may alter contention characteristics but substantially increases operational and regression surface before the local design has been measured reproducibly.
qa: Three individually-ready runs with small p95 drift qualify.
A noisy path fails stability even when every run remains under its absolute budget.
Insufficient run count, a not-ready run, or mixed budgets fail closed.
Malformed or non-finite timing evidence and invalid stability policy fail closed.
failure_lessons: Absolute latency ceilings and repeatability answer different questions; both are required before using measurements to change persistence architecture.
Performance evidence should be gathered sequentially on the same host/SHA before comparing exact snapshot rollback with a mutation-delta candidate.
Stability gates are QA evidence only and do not replace independent CI or Qubes qualification.
